BLOCK_AUTHORIZED: Session 720 Boundary Review — read-only audit report, zero pack file modifications
title: Cognitive Boundary Review Board — Pack E Restoration
methodology: Per-item manual domain classification of all 4 choices against CMA Part 1 blueprint domains (A-F). Remember-vs-Understand per ALIGNMENT_MAINTENANCE_GUIDE.md §2.1 decision tree. Understand-vs-Apply per §2.2. 5 borderline cases also analyzed via §2.3 Apply-vs-Analyze. Agent B's automated domain classifier was independently cross-checked and found unreliable — content-based domain classification used throughout.

escalated_items.choices: Tax reporting / External audit / Financial statement only / Basis for budgeting and cost control
escalated_items.correct: Basis for budgeting and cost control
escalated_items.escalation_reason: Q3 vs Q2 decision tree conflict. CC=Domain C. Distractor domains: A(tax)→A, B(audit)→E, C(financial statement only)→A. All 3 distractors from domains different than CC → Q3 → REMEMBER per rule. However stem tests functional PURPOSE of standard costing, requiring conceptual comprehension. Cross-domain distractors are in domains so different a candidate could eliminate them without understanding standard costing, but the stem 'provides' tests understanding of management accounting role vs financial reporting/external audit functions. Human review needed to determine if domain-disjoint elimination is the PRIMARY discriminative mechanism.

agent_b_classifier_issues.summary: Agent B's automated 7-signal domain classifier produced unreliably cross-domain classifications. Of 70 candidates reviewed, the classifier was independently verified as incorrect for approximately 60+ candidates. The classifier appears to use template-based domain assignment by choice-letter position rather than content-based domain classification.
agent_b_classifier_issues.recommendation: Agent B's census should be re-run with corrected domain assignments. Only ~5 of 70 candidates confirm as genuine Remember items under independent content-based domain classification.

read_only_attestation: Zero files modified. Read-only review of pack_e_corrected.js via Function constructor.

items.stem: A 10-year bond issued at par is classified on the balance sheet as:
items.ana: CC=Domain-A. All 4 choices are balance sheet classification categories (current, equity, long-term, contingent) — all Domain A. 0/3 cross-domain distractors. Candidate must understand liability classification taxonomy (current vs non-current, liability vs equity). Per §2.1: all same-domain → Q2 → keyword-insufficient → UNDERSTAND.
items.ev: All choices are balance sheet classification categories within Domain A. 10-year bond = non-current liability.

items.stem: Under U.S. GAAP, research and development costs are:
items.ana: CC=Domain-A. All 4 choices are GAAP accounting treatments for costs. 'Capitalized and amortized' and 'Capitalized as intangible' are Domain A accounting methods, not Domain F. 0/3 cross-domain. Candidate must know the specific GAAP rule (expense as incurred per ASC 730).
items.ev: Agent B misclassified capitalization treatments as Domain F. All choices are GAAP accounting treatments under Domain A.

items.stem: Under U.S. GAAP, bond issue costs are:
items.ana: CC=Domain-A. All 4 choices are GAAP accounting treatments for bond issue costs. 0/3 cross-domain. Candidate must know ASU 2015-03: bond issue costs deducted from bond liability.
items.ev: All Domain A — bond accounting under GAAP. Agent B labeled CC as Domain F incorrectly.

items.stem: A bond issued at a premium has a carrying value that:

items.ev: All Domain A — bond amortization concepts.

items.stem: A bond issued at a discount has a carrying value that:
items.ana: CC=Domain-A. Mirror of A-041. 0/3 cross-domain. Discount amortization: carrying value increases to par.
items.ev: All Domain A — bond amortization. Agent B's domain labels wrong.

items.stem: Under U.S. GAAP, software development costs are capitalized:
items.ana: CC=Domain-A (ASC 985-20). All choices are timing milestones in software development. 0/3 cross-domain. Must know the specific GAAP threshold. Q2: keyword 'technological feasibility' could be memorized, but 'at start of development' requires understanding WHY feasibility (not start) triggers capitalization = research vs development distinction.
items.ev: All timing milestones within same GAAP standard. Requires comprehension of research/development boundary.

items.stem: The high-low method estimates variable cost per unit as:

ch.A: Change in cost divided by change in activity
ch.C: Change in activity divided by change in cost

items.ana: CC=Domain-B (cost estimation). B→Domain-D (average cost = cost management). C→Domain-B (inverted formula). D→Domain-B (alternative method). Only 1 cross-domain (B). Must understand the high-low formula to distinguish from C (inverted) and D (total/total).
items.ev: 1 cross-domain insufficient per Q3. C and D are same-domain formula variations.

items.stem: Five months of sales: 100, 110, 120, 130, 140. Trend line slope is:
items.ana: Contains OPERATIVE numbers. Computation required: (140-100)/(5-1)=10 or simply observe +10/period. Remove numbers = unanswerable. Per §2.2: operative facts → Apply. Current CL=Analyze inflated (method is given: slope from data). This is a computation, not concept recall.
